scope: Spline correction_method BinByBin, acceptance bin-by-bin only. 3D phi_h in the copy of fits/spline/correction_method/BinByBin/fit_copy.root, Q2-y 1-17, 452 histograms. The file has rdf, mdf, gdf, Acceptance, Background, and Bin histograms and no Bayesian, RC_Bayesian, BC_RC_Bayesian, or 5D histograms. Those families were not created. No publication. The source fit, budgets, sector exclusions, and the shared Phi_h guides were not edited. This copy does not replace the source. The destination did not already contain refinement_note.json and fit.json, so this is not a resume.
start_mode: manual. start=auto: the 3D spline B windows selected by these histograms have median width 0.0153 and 428 of 452 are narrower than 0.05, and the C windows are narrower (median 0.0070, 445 of 452 narrower than 0.05), so they can pin a fit. The run-local guide started as Phi_h_Fit_Parameters_Initialize.py. --use_spline_init was not passed.
changed: Pass 1 refit all 452 histograms with the manual baseline and the corrected filled-window range. It made 20 worse. The worst was (Q2_y_Bin_3)-(z_pT_Bin_16), because that manual key has no B or C start: the fitter kept the broad initializer and the second pass only moved halfway, with B collapsing near -0.061. (Q2_y_Bin_1)-(z_pT_Bin_8) did not move. Its cosine is B=-0.03073, inside the manual window [-0.05, 0.05], so that limit was not opened. Pass 2 put 67 starts on each histogram's own unconstrained cosine, used limits +/-0.15 in B and +/-0.10 in C, and turned off the half-amplitude second window. That removed the large chi-squared misses. Pass 3 did the same for 98 histograms whose second-pass window was still narrower than the unconstrained cosine error, or whose chi-squared was still at least 0.3 above that cosine, including (Q2_y_Bin_16)-(z_pT_Bin_14) and (Q2_y_Bin_8)-(z_pT_Bin_21), where a near-zero B had an error below 0.001. Every Q2-y bin was in that set, so the remake covered Q2-y 1-17. JSON still has 452 bins. Histogram contents are unchanged. No range mismatch. 36 histograms have a lower chi-squared than the stored fit and none is worse (largest increase 0.0001). The largest drop is (Q2_y_Bin_13)-(z_pT_Bin_10), chi-squared 112.229 to 93.922. (1, 8) stays at B=-0.030730, statistical error 0.022844, C=0.015188, error 0.011380, chi-squared 25.154, NDF 13, status completed, phi 60-300, 16 histogram bins inside the TF1 range. That is this histogram's cosine, not the nominal B=-0.125184.
left_bins: No 5D family is in this file, so nothing was left from a 3D-versus-5D disagreement. Large nominal-minus-variation shifts were not pulled onto the nominal. They stay on this histogram's cosine. (Q2_y_Bin_1)-(z_pT_Bin_15) did move, from the stored B=-0.05903 to its own cosine, and is still far from the nominal: (Q2_y_Bin_1)-(z_pT_Bin_8) B=-0.03073 versus nominal -0.12518; (Q2_y_Bin_1)-(z_pT_Bin_1) B=-0.04759 versus nominal -0.11513; (Q2_y_Bin_1)-(z_pT_Bin_15) B=-0.05246 versus nominal -0.11743; (Q2_y_Bin_5)-(z_pT_Bin_18) B=-0.37229 versus nominal -0.43158; (Q2_y_Bin_3)-(z_pT_Bin_29) B=-0.23041 versus nominal -0.27991. (Q2_y_Bin_1)-(z_pT_Bin_8) keeps B=-0.030730 rather than the nominal B=-0.125184 because the points support the smaller modulation. The shift relative to the nominal statistical error is large, and it was not shrunk. Excluded sector pairs were not put back into this comparison. No comparison was filled with zero. The source was not removed from the budget, and fit-parameter errors were not added to the systematic uncertainty.
